name: dashboard-shell
description: Application dashboard layout with sidebar navigation, header, and content area

sidebar.description: Collapsible sidebar containing logo, navigation, and user avatar

nav.description: Primary navigation container within the sidebar

nav-item.description: Individual navigation link with optional icon and badge

header.description: Top header bar with search, notifications, and user menu

logo.description: Application logo displayed at the top of the sidebar

search.description: Search input area within the header

user-menu.description: User dropdown menu area in the header

content.description: Main content area for dashboard pages

footer.description: Optional footer at the bottom of the content area

sidebar-toggle.description: Button that opens and closes the off-canvas sidebar below the md floor; hidden from md up, where the sidebar is docked and there is no drawer to open. Wire it with directives, no controller: a drawer flag in the root's l-data, @click="drawer = !drawer" and :aria-expanded on the toggle (aria-controls names the sidebar's id), :data-state="drawer ? 'expanded' : null" on the sidebar

nav-label.description: Text of a nav-item, hidden when the sidebar is collapsed

sidebar-user.description: Account block pinned to the foot of the sidebar

metric.description: A single KPI figure inside a content card

activity-item.description: One entry of the activity feed inside a content card

default.description: Standard dashboard view with expanded sidebar

a11y.notes: Ship the sidebar WITHOUT a data-state: from the md floor up it is a docked grid column whatever its state, and below md an absent state is the closed off-canvas drawer. data-state="expanded" in static markup opens that drawer as a fixed overlay over a phone's content. The toggle is a real <button type="button"> with aria-controls and aria-expanded kept in step with the drawer; a closed drawer is visibility: hidden, so its links are out of the tab order.

keyboard.Escape: close open dropdown menus, and the phone drawer (an @keydown.escape on the root)

templates.html:
{logo}
{item}
{header}
{content}
{footer}

changes.note: The reference markup and template no longer ship data-state="expanded" on the sidebar, which opened the off-canvas drawer as a fixed overlay over a phone with no way to close it: the sidebar is docked from md up whatever its state, and an absent state is the closed drawer below md. The default variant wires its sidebar-toggle with directives (a drawer flag in l-data, @click, :aria-expanded, :data-state, Escape closes) and the toggle is hidden from md up, where there is no drawer. Markup that sets data-state itself is unchanged.
Give the collapsed rail's navigation the available inline size, center its glyphs, and hide label-dependent badges so no navigation box is clipped past the viewport start.
Use the AA-gated muted foreground for visible footer text instead of the decorative subtle foreground.

The responsive ladder moves onto the breakpoint canon, mobile-first (task 0.8-09). The sheet's max-width media blocks became min-width floors on canon tiers (sm 40rem/640px, md 48rem/768px, lg 64rem/1024px), so every unconditional rule is now the PHONE case and a tier block only ever widens it. The off-canvas drawer is now the base and the sidebar rejoins the grid at md — the same 768px floor as before. The two :has(sidebar collapsed) rules moved into the md block, fixing a pre-canon bug: at (0,3,0) they outranked the single-column rule at (0,1,0), so a collapsed sidebar on a phone produced a 4rem column no grid area was ever placed in. The floors keep their values, so the only behavioural shift is at exactly a floor: 1024px now gets the wide layout rather than the narrow one.
